afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 221150
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
450 AM MST Tue Sep 22 2026

.UPDATE...Updated 12Z Aviation Discussion.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Rain chances return to portions of Eastern Arizona starting 
  today, with most activity focused over foothill and high terrain
  areas.

- Best chances to see lower desert rainfall will occur on 
  Wednesday, but otherwise, most of the activity should remain to 
  the north and east of the Phoenix metro through the end of the 
  work week.

- Near to slightly above normal temperatures will persist over 
  the next several days. 
  
&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Wednesday/...
Current RAP analysis reveals shortwave ridging over the Rockies as 
flanking waves spin near the Great Lakes and Great Basin. The latter 
of these disturbances will be the main weather focus over the Desert 
Southwest through at least the middle portion of the week, helping 
to renew rain chances during the waning days of monsoon season. 
Even though southwesterly flow will persist, which typically 
translate to rather benign conditions across the region, the 
Pacific low will be strong/deep enough to help pull sub-tropical 
moisture upwards into eastern Arizona today, with PWATs increasing
toward 150- 175% of normal. Combine this moisture with positive 
vorticity advection and a developing upper-level jet streak, and 
you get an environment favorable for shower and isolated 
thunderstorm development. However, with a sharp east-west cutoff 
of sufficient moisture expected, most, if not all, rainfall 
activity will be confined to the easternmost third of Arizona, and
therefore, coverage over our area will be focused primarily over 
Gila County. With this setup and better synoptic support, rounds 
of showers and isolated of storms will be possible from mid-
morning into the early nighttime hours as the environment will not
be solely reliant on surface heating and orographic influences, 
which typically limit warm season activity to the afternoon and 
evening hours. Due to the potential to see multiple instances of 
rain over the same areas, minor flooding will be the main concern,
especially if a specific locations experiences several heavier 
cells. 

One forecast aspect that will need to monitored later this evening 
will be the potential for areas of blowing dust in lower deserts of 
Pinal and Maricopa Counties due to gusty southeasterly outflow winds 
from distant showers and storms. Hi-res data is highlighting this 
potential and with a dry boundary layer in place, DCAPE values will 
near or exceed 1000 J/kg, making this outcome not so far-fetched,
even though this is not your typical blowing dust signal. 
However, dust generation will be heavily dependent on if strong 
enough convection can become established. At the very minimum, the
southeasterly flow will help increase boundary layer moisture 
Tuesday night, which could set the stage for further activity on 
Wednesday. 

Speaking of Wednesday, the southwestern wave is shown splitting 
in two separate areas of energy, with one area being ejected 
toward the Northern Plains, while another area lingers off the 
Baja Coast. The latter area will tilt regional flow more out of 
the south and perhaps even slightly southeasterly, helping to 
nudge moisture further west over the lower deserts. This, along 
with the previously mentioned low-level moisture increase, has 
caused a shift in the forecast compared to 24 hours ago, with the 
NBM now indicating the better potential for rainfall over South-
central Arizona will now be on Wednesday as opposed to Thursday. 
Though the moisture may still be in place, with the low now 
significantly weaker, and the aforementioned jet streak migrating 
further north, the synoptic setup becomes much less favorable to 
see rainfall outside of the typical enhanced terrain areas. One 
wildcard though is the projected presence of a 700mb wave moving 
up out of Northern Mexico Wednesday morning. Current forecast 
tracks have this kink progressing near the Arizona/New Mexico 
border, which would likely provide better support for rainfall 
once again for areas further east of here. With that being said, 
any subtle changes to trough evolution could yield shower and 
thunderstorms for lower desert areas, which is likely why 20-30% 
PoPs are indicated for Phoenix as the rainfall potential cannot be
completely ignored.

Even will that, temperatures have not been mentioned. Highs across 
the region will not vary too much compared to what we have seen the 
past few days with readings running near to slightly above normal. 
Lower deserts can expected MaxTs around 93-102 degrees while higher 
elevation locations will experience temps closer to the lower 80s to 
lower 90s. 

&&

.LONG TERM /Thursday through Monday/... 
Heading into the back half of the week, the influence from the 
previously-mentioned low will continue to diminish, but sufficient-
enough moisture for further rain chances will remain in place, at 
least through Thursday. NBM/WPC continue to paint Eastern an 
Northern Arizona in decent PoPs (30-60%), including our portion of 
Gila County, thanks to orographic influences, but synoptic support 
will be all but gone by this point, so desert chances drop back to 
generally below 20%, but not all the way zero. PWATs 100-150% of 
normal are likely why non-zero PoPs are shown for the lower 
elevations, but unless you find yourself around enhanced terrain 
features such as the Kofas or Table Top Wilderness, another rainfall 
should not be counted on at this point. Gradual drying begin on 
Saturday, but it may not remain that way for too long as we may 
start to see fringe moisture associated with Hurricane Polo by as
early as the weekend. Forecast confidence regarding where this 
tropical cyclone will progress in the longer term is low, and 
there will likely be many forecast changes regarding it in the 
coming day, but its potential influence will be monitored 
regardless over through the remainder of the week.

In term of temperatures, much like during the short term, not much 
fluctuation in day-to-day readings is expected to occur. Daily 
values will hover right around to just above normal, which 
translates to lower desert readings ranging between 94-105 degrees 
through the weekend. Overnight lows will be slightly more elevated 
compared to where they typically are for late September, likely an 
effect of lingering moisture and cloud cover (at least for some 
spots), with readings between 70-82 degrees. Meanwhile higher 
elevation conditions will be quite comfortable as most locations 
should be in the 80s, with perhaps a few spots touching the lower 
90s. Lows for these spots in the upper 50s to lower 70s will be 
common.  

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1150Z. 

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 

Primary aviation impact will be the potential for VCSH/VCTS
Tuesday evening and gusty outflow winds. Light E'rly winds will
continue through the morning before an extended period of S'rly
winds this afternoon. Confidence in a W/SW shift late this
afternoon/early this evening remains low. It has been added to the
KDVT TAF for a few hours, but remains out of the other three
sites for now. SHRA/TSRA activity is expected to develop this
afternoon and evening, but is expected to remain south and east of
the Phoenix Metro with a low chance (10%) of some isolated
activity within the metro. However, confidence is good that a
SE'rly outflow will move through the metro this evening, with
current timing around 02-03Z. Confidence is lower on how high
wind speeds will be and if there is any reductions in VIS from
BLDU. TEMPO groups remain in the KPHX and KIWA TAFs for some gusts
up around 20-25 kt this evening. There remains a low chance (5-10%)
for gusts of 30+ kts with the outflow. FEW to SCT clouds will be
common through the TAF period with lowest bases around 8-10 kft
AGL. There will also be increasing high clouds (around 25 kft)
through the period and should become BKN by this afternoon. 

Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 

No major aviation impacts are anticipated through the next 24 
hours with mostly clear skies. Winds will favor W/NW at both KIPL
and KBLH, with wind speeds mostly staying below 10 kts and periods
of light and variable winds.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Near to slightly above normal temperatures will prevail over the 
next several days, with minimal day-to-day fluctuations. Daily
rain chances return for the high terrain through the end of the 
workweek with lower desert chances focused on Wednesday. MinRHs 
between 15-30% will be common across the region through the start
of the weekend, with even higher readings (35-50%) for the far 
eastern districts. MaxRHs will range from fair to good over the 
western and central districts, to good and excellent for the 
eastern districts into the weekend. Drier air by the weekend will
lower RHs slightly, but they should remain above critical fire
weather thresholds. Outside of any thunderstorm related outflows,
winds will follow familiar diurnal trends with typical terrain 
induced afternoon gusts around 15-25 mph. 

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.
&&

$$

SHORT TERM...RW
LONG TERM...RW 
AVIATION...Berislavich/Benedict
FIRE WEATHER...RW
